text: The web app follows links to other servers and expands linked graphs in place
description:
Felix 2026-11-12: servers allow requests from other origins, so that the web app can follow everywhere and expand sub-graphs to everywhere. The website uses the API at a graph's host URL to load that server's graph data.

The browser loads a linked graph directly from the server hosting it; the server of the graph being viewed never fetches foreign graphs. Clicking the node of a linked graph expands its ideas in place, read-only unless the viewer has rights there.

A linked graph that cannot be reached, Felix 2026-11-12: the link is still there, so the node is still shown. Trying to expand it shows something like "not available"; maybe the server is just down.

Value and priority, decided by Felix 2026-11-12:
- Value: as it is normalized, the node of a contributing graph works with whatever flows to it from the host graph. That value is distributed in proportion to the intrinsic values of the contributing graph. Later the host graph might be allowed a bias, but that might complicate things.
- Priority only looks at the host graph. It stops at contributing graphs.

Changes the rule of 2026-09-20 (e81b11c3; a82b1530 was cancelled for it): a linked graph was one opaque node whose ideas are never drawn. Claude's reading: the stored link stays a link to the whole graph, and only the view opens it. e81b11c3 stays as the record of what was built.

Security: a server lets pages from other addresses read its graphs; a login on one server gives no rights on another, and a foreign page must not be able to write in a visitor's name.

Felix: this implicitly solves the scaling problem.

Related: bd1cefe0 (partial rendering, halted); 3023ebec (linked graph as a sink for value).

supportingConnections.hypothesis: With an outline, people can tell external ideas from their own at a glance.
The red arrow says why the drop does nothing, so nobody makes connections that can't be stored.
supportingConnections.reflection: In part: the code now refuses those drops and shows the red arrow (tested). Whether people understand the red as 'not across graphs' hasn't been watched in use.

supportingConnections.hypothesis: Linking support right where the other graph is open is quicker than going through the settings dialog.
supportingConnections.reflection: Mechanically yes: one drag now writes the link that used to take the idea's edit dialog. It works only for a graph already linked to some idea here, since an outline appears only for a graph that is open in place.

status.comment: 8b945c1f: clicking a linked graph's node loads its ideas in the browser from the server hosting it and hangs them below the node (read-only, click on one opens the graph on its server, click on the node closes it). Value: the inflow takes the place of the linked graph's whole intrinsic value and flows along its own connections; priority stays in the host graph. An unreachable graph keeps its node, labelled '(not available)'. Tests: shared graph-host.test.ts, frontend data-linked-graph-view.spec.ts, pnpm check 25/25. Open: editing in place where the viewer has rights on the other server (always read-only now); expanding graphs linked inside an opened graph; not tried live between two running servers (cross-origin read).
